mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, observed over the last week, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A substantial week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, as seen in the last week, indicates a return to office work that will directly translate into increased retail and recreation activity during lunch breaks and after-work hours over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES increasing by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in TRANSIT mobility suggests a shift in daily routines where more people are commuting and spending less time at home, which will lead to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, even when RESIDENTIAL mobility falls and TRANSIT mobility rises concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of loosening public health restrictions, the consistent decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility from its peak indicates a return to more diverse shopping patterns, diverting activity towards retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility continuing its downward trend in a loosening restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility, especially after a period of increase, signals a reduction in outdoor leisure activities, which will divert discretionary spending away from related retail and recreation over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 0.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, despite PARKS mobility falling by more than 0.5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based increase in mobility across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RETAIL_REC in the most recent week indicates a strong underlying momentum for economic re-engagement, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while WORKPLACES mobility experiences a significant drop, it indicates a reversal in the trend of returning to work and increased time spent at home, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 10 and WORKPLACES falls by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% and WORKPLACES mobility drops by more than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: As the season transitions to colder weather in mid-October, the natural decline in outdoor activities, reflected in PARKS mobility, will lead to a general reduction in discretionary outdoor retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite the seasonal shift and a decline in PARKS mobility.
